notes.official: **The chapter opens on a sound-bridge.** עָרוּם arum ('shrewd') and עֲרוּמִּים arummim ('naked', the closing word of 2:25) share consonants but not roots — the wordplay is sonic, not etymological. Genesis is deliberate: nakedness-without-shame in 2:25 hands directly into shrewdness-without-disclosure in 3:1. The serpent is *cleverer* than any field-animal — note YHWH-Elohim is named as the maker — and his clever turn is rhetorical: he opens with a *question* that misquotes the original prohibition. 2:17 said the human (singular) might not eat from *one* tree; the serpent's question generalizes to *any* tree. The reframing forces the woman to defend the prohibition — and in defending it, in v3, she adds her own hedge to it. Note also that the serpent uses bare *Elohim*, not the compound *YHWH-Elohim* used by the narrator. The personal-name distance is the serpent's first move.

notes.official: **Three slips in the woman's quotation.** First, *and you shall not touch it*: nothing in the original prohibition (2:17) addresses touch — only eating. The woman has added a fence to the commandment. Second, *lest you die* (פֶּן־תְּמֻתֻן pen-temutun): the original was מוֹת תָּמוּת mot tamut 'you shall surely die' — the infinitive-absolute intensifier removed, the certainty softened to a contingent fear. Third, the tree is described only as *the one in the midst of the garden* — not by its actual identifier (the tree of knowing good and bad). The woman is paraphrasing from a distance, and the serpent will exploit the looseness in the next verse. The original command, of course, was given to the human alone (2:16–17), before the woman was built (2:22) — she received it secondhand.

notes.official: *Lo mot temutun* — **you shall surely not die**. The serpent mirrors YHWH-Elohim's grammar exactly: the infinitive absolute מוֹת mot before the finite verb תְּמֻתוּן temutun, intensifying — but with the negation לֹא lo placed *before* the infinitive absolute itself. The strict grammatical reading is not 'you shall not surely die' (uncertainty about death) but 'you shall *surely not* die' (certainty about not-death). The serpent is not hedging; he is asserting the opposite certainty. The construction is unusual — placing לֹא before the infinitive absolute is rare and emphatic. The next verse will give the reason: not because death is unreal, but because the consequence YHWH-Elohim named is, the serpent claims, a cover story.

notes.official:
**The chapter's keystone verse.** The serpent's claim has three components, each of which the chapter will independently confirm.

*Beyom acholchem ... v'niphqecho eineichem* — **on the day you eat ... your eyes will be opened**. Confirmed at v7: 'the eyes of the two of them were opened'. The verb פָּקַח paqach is the same in both — the serpent's promise and the narrative's report use identical vocabulary. The eyes do open.

*Vihyitem ke-elohim* — **you will be like the Elohim**. Confirmed at v22 by YHWH-Elohim's own words: 'the human has become *like one of us*'. The serpent's promise of class-elevation is not refuted — it is acknowledged from above.

*Yodei tov vara* — **knowing good and bad**. Confirmed at v22, same phrase, same root יָדַע yada. The contested knowledge is granted.

What the serpent gets *wrong* — or omits — is the second consequence: that the opening of eyes also opens shame, that the class-rise costs the garden, that knowing comes with mortality surfacing. The serpent's three claims are all literally true; his lie is one of omission. The traditional reading that 'the serpent lies' has to either spiritualize the deaths-by-mortality the chapter delivers or contest the verses themselves; the simpler reading is that everything the serpent says happens, *and* the warnings YHWH-Elohim gave are also true. Both are.

i18n.es: Y la mujer vio que el árbol era bueno para comer, que era un deleite para los ojos, y que el árbol era deseable para obtener entendimiento; y tomó de su fruto y comió. También dio a su marido con ella, y él comió.
i18n.fr: La femme vit que l'arbre était bon à manger, qu'il était un délice pour les yeux, et que l'arbre était désirable pour acquérir le discernement ; et elle prit de son fruit et en mangea. Elle en donna aussi à son mari avec elle, et il en mangea.
i18n.ja: 女は、その木が食べるに良く、目に喜ばしく、また知恵を得るに望ましいことを見た。そして彼女はその実を取って食べ、また共にいた夫にも与え、彼も食べた。
i18n.ko: 여자가 보니 그 나무는 먹기에 좋고, 눈에 즐거움이며, 통찰을 얻기에 탐스러운 나무였다; 그래서 그녀는 그 열매를 따서 먹었다. 그녀는 또한 자기와 함께 있는 남편에게도 주었고, 그도 먹었다.
i18n.ru: И увидела женщина, что дерево хорошо для пищи, и что оно отрада для глаз, и что дерево желанно для обретения разумения; и взяла от плода его, и ела. И дала также мужу своему с нею, и он ел.
i18n.zh: 女人见那树的果子适合作食物，悦人眼目，又是可喜爱的，能使人得着洞见；就摘下果子来吃了。她也给了和她在一起的丈夫，他也吃了。
i18n.zh-Hant: 女人看見那樹的果子宜於食用、悅人眼目，又是渴慕之物可使人有見識；她便摘下果子吃了，又給她身旁的丈夫，他也吃了。

notes.official:
**Three goods, then the act.** The tree is *good for food*, *a delight to the eyes*, and *desirable for gaining insight* — the triple description echoes the language of chapter 1, where the Elohim repeatedly saw that what was made was *good*. The woman applies the same evaluative grammar to the tree she has been told not to eat from. The act follows judgment, not appetite.

*She also gave to her husband **with her***. The phrase עִמָּהּ immah ('with her') is structurally crucial: the man is *present*, not off in another part of the garden. He is beside her through the serpent-dialogue, the seeing, the taking. The reading tradition that imagines Adam absent and the woman alone-with-the-serpent has to ignore the immah. He is there. The decision is hers (she sees, she takes, she eats); the agreement is his (he eats, with no recorded objection). His subsequent claim in v12 ('the woman whom you gave to be with me — she gave me') will be technically accurate and morally insufficient.

paragraphs.text: וַתִּפָּקַ֙חְנָה֙ עֵינֵ֣י שְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיֵּ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֥י עֵֽירֻמִּ֖ם הֵ֑ם וַֽיִּתְפְּרוּ֙ עֲלֵ֣ה תְאֵנָ֔ה וַיַּעֲשׂ֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם חֲגֹרֹֽת׃

i18n.en: Then the eyes of the two of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together and made for themselves belts.
i18n.he: וַתִּפָּקַ֙חְנָה֙ עֵינֵ֣י שְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיֵּ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֥י עֵֽירֻמִּ֖ם הֵ֑ם וַֽיִּתְפְּרוּ֙ עֲלֵ֣ה תְאֵנָ֔ה וַיַּעֲשׂ֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם חֲגֹרֹֽת׃
i18n.de: Da gingen den beiden die Augen auf, und sie erkannten, daß sie nackt waren; und sie hefteten Feigenblätter zusammen und machten sich Gürtel.
i18n.es: Entonces se abrieron los ojos de los dos, y supieron que estaban desnudos; y cosieron hojas de higuera juntas y se hicieron ceñidores.
i18n.fr: Alors les yeux des deux s'ouvrirent, et ils surent qu'ils étaient nus ; ils cousirent ensemble des feuilles de figuier et se firent des ceintures.
i18n.ja: すると二人の目は開かれ、自分たちが裸であることを知った。彼らはいちじくの葉を縫い合わせ、自分たちのために帯を造った。
i18n.ko: 그러자 그 둘의 눈이 열려, 자기들이 벗은 것을 알게 되었다; 그래서 무화과 잎을 엮어 자기들을 위해 허리띠를 만들었다.
i18n.ru: И открылись глаза у обоих, и узнали они, что наги; и сшили листья смоковницы и сделали себе пояса.
i18n.zh: 他们二人的眼睛就开了，便知道自己是赤身露体；他们就缝起无花果树叶，为自己作了腰带。
i18n.zh-Hant: 於是他們二人的眼睛都開了，知道自己是赤身的；他們便將無花果樹的葉子縫合在一起，為自己作了腰帶。

notes.official:
**The promise opens, the nakedness closes.** The first half of v7 fulfills the serpent's promise word for word — same verb, same construction. The second half completes the arc from 2:25: they were naked and unashamed; now they are naked and aware of it. The *knowing* (יָדַע yada) here is exactly the kind the tree was named for — experiential acquaintance with their own condition. The first thing they know with their newly-opened eyes is themselves.

*Belts* (חֲגֹרֹת chagorot), not *aprons* (KJV) or *loincloths* (NRSV): the noun is from חָגַר chagar 'to gird', and refers to a wraparound waist-garment. The improvisation is partial — the chest and limbs are uncovered — and YHWH-Elohim will upgrade the covering substantially in v21.

paragraphs.text: וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֞וּ אֶת־ק֨וֹל יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים מִתְהַלֵּ֥ךְ בַּגָּ֖ן לְר֣וּחַ הַיּ֑וֹם וַיִּתְחַבֵּ֨א הָֽאָדָ֜ם וְאִשְׁתּ֗וֹ מִפְּנֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֔ים בְּת֖וֹךְ עֵ֥ץ הַגָּֽן׃

i18n.en: They heard the voice of YHWH-Elohim walking about in the garden at the breeze of the day; and the human and his woman hid themselves from the face of YHWH-Elohim among the trees of the garden.
i18n.he: וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֞וּ אֶת־ק֨וֹל יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים מִתְהַלֵּ֥ךְ בַּגָּ֖ן לְר֣וּחַ הַיּ֑וֹם וַיִּתְחַבֵּ֨א הָֽאָדָ֜ם וְאִשְׁתּ֗וֹ מִפְּנֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֔ים בְּת֖וֹךְ עֵ֥ץ הַגָּֽן׃
i18n.de: Sie hörten die Stimme YHWH Elohims, die im Garten umherging beim Wehen des Tages; und der Mensch und seine Frau verbargen sich vor dem Angesicht YHWH Elohims unter den Bäumen des Gartens.
i18n.es: Y oyeron la voz de YHWH Elohim paseándose por el jardín al fresco del día; y el ser humano y su mujer se escondieron de la faz de YHWH Elohim entre los árboles del jardín.
i18n.fr: Ils entendirent la voix de YHWH Elohim qui se promenait dans le jardin à la brise du jour ; et l'être humain et sa femme se cachèrent de la face de YHWH Elohim parmi les arbres du jardin.
i18n.ja: 彼らは、日の風の吹くころ、園を歩き回る YHWH エロヒムの声を聞いた。そして人とその女は、YHWH エロヒムの顔を避けて、園の木々の間に身を隠した。
i18n.ko: 그들은 날이 서늘할 때 동산을 거니시는 YHWH 엘로힘의 소리를 들었다; 그리고 사람과 그의 여자는 동산 나무들 사이에 YHWH 엘로힘의 얼굴을 피하여 숨었다.
i18n.ru: И услышали они голос YHWH Элохим, ходящих по саду в прохладе дня; и спрятались человек и жена его от лица YHWH Элохим среди деревьев сада.
i18n.zh: 他们听见 YHWH 厄罗音在天起凉风时于园中走动的声音；那人与他的女人便藏在园中的树木之间，躲避 YHWH 厄罗音的面。
i18n.zh-Hant: 他們聽見 YHWH 厄羅音在天起涼風時，行走於園中的聲音；那人和他的女人便藏身於園中的樹木之間，躲避 YHWH 厄羅音的面。

notes.official:
**The mode of divine presence.** *Mithallech* — the hithpael of הָלַךְ — is iterative *walking about*, the same form used of Enoch (5:22, 24) and Noah (6:9) walking-about *with* the Elohim. The picture is at-home: YHWH-Elohim is not visiting the garden but moving through it as resident. The disruption isn't the arrival of a stranger but the changed posture of the hosts.

*L'ruach ha-yom* — **at the breeze of the day**. רוּחַ ruach (the breath/wind/spirit of 1:2) returns. In construct with יוֹם 'day' it points to the evening wind that rises when the heat falls — the time of relief. The garden's daily rhythm is intact; only the humans inside it have shifted. The chapter's keynote of perceptual change holds in geography too: yesterday's familiar sound is today's signal to hide.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְרָ֛א יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־הָֽאָדָ֑ם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ אַיֶּֽכָּה׃

i18n.en: YHWH-Elohim called to the human and said to him, "Where are you?"
i18n.he: וַיִּקְרָ֛א יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־הָֽאָדָ֑ם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ אַיֶּֽכָּה׃
i18n.de: YHWH Elohim riefen dem Menschen zu und sprachen zu ihm: "Wo bist du?"
i18n.es: YHWH Elohim llamó al ser humano y le dijo: «¿Dónde estás?»
i18n.fr: YHWH Elohim appela l'être humain et lui dit : « Où es-tu ? »
i18n.ja: YHWH エロヒムは人に呼びかけて言った、「お前はどこにいるのか」。
i18n.ko: YHWH 엘로힘이 사람을 부르며 말씀하셨다, "네가 어디 있느냐?"
i18n.ru: И воззвали YHWH Элохим к человеку и сказали ему: «Где ты?»
i18n.zh: YHWH 厄罗音呼唤那人，对他说：「你在哪里？」
i18n.zh-Hant: YHWH 厄羅音呼喚那人，對他說：「你在哪裡？」

notes.official: *Ayekka* — **where are you?** A single word in Hebrew, the interrogative אֵי 'where' fused with the 2ms suffix. The question opens a chain (v11 'who told you?', v13 'what is this you have done?', v14 implicit 'what have *you* done?') that has the shape of a judicial inquiry — but also the shape of pastoral pursuit. The Hebrew settles neither register. The human's reply does not actually answer the question — he names what he *heard* (the voice), what he *was* (afraid), what he *did* (hid), and what he was not (clothed). Of his location: nothing.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אֶת־קֹלְךָ֥ שָׁמַ֖עְתִּי בַּגָּ֑ן וָאִירָ֛א כִּֽי־עֵירֹ֥ם אָנֹ֖כִי וָאֵחָבֵֽא׃

i18n.en: He said, "I heard your voice in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked; and I hid myself."
i18n.he: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אֶת־קֹלְךָ֥ שָׁמַ֖עְתִּי בַּגָּ֑ן וָאִירָ֛א כִּֽי־עֵירֹ֥ם אָנֹ֖כִי וָאֵחָבֵֽא׃
i18n.de: Er sprach: "Ich hörte deine Stimme im Garten, und ich fürchtete mich, weil ich nackt war; und ich verbarg mich."
i18n.es: Él dijo: «Oí tu voz en el jardín, y tuve miedo porque estaba desnudo; y me escondí».
i18n.fr: Il dit : « J'ai entendu ta voix dans le jardin, et j'ai eu peur parce que j'étais nu ; et je me suis caché. »
i18n.ja: 彼は言った、「わたしは園であなたの声を聞き、裸であったので恐れて、身を隠したのです」。
i18n.ko: 그가 말하였다, "제가 동산에서 당신의 소리를 듣고, 벗었기에 두려워하여 숨었습니다."
i18n.ru: И он сказал: «Голос Твой я услышал в саду и убоялся, ибо я наг; и спрятался».
i18n.zh: 他说：「我在园中听见你的声音，就害怕，因为我赤身露体；我便藏起来了。」
i18n.zh-Hant: 他說：「我在園中聽見祢的聲音，我就害怕，因為我赤身；我便藏了起來。」

notes.official: **The first fear in the narrative, and it is misdiagnosed.** The human answers the *ayekka* (v9) with a confession that names the wrong problem: *I was afraid because I was naked, and I hid*. יָרֵא *yare*, "afraid", enters the story here — fear arrives as a response to the maker's approach. But the stated cause is off. Nothing about the nakedness changed; they were naked and unashamed in 2:25. What changed is the knowledge that now interprets it. The human reports the symptom (exposure) and conceals the act (eating), and the hiding is itself the tell: one hides from a threat, and the human has recast his maker as one.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מִ֚י הִגִּ֣יד לְךָ֔ כִּ֥י עֵירֹ֖ם אָ֑תָּה הֲמִן־הָעֵ֗ץ אֲשֶׁ֧ר צִוִּיתִ֛יךָ לְבִלְתִּ֥י אֲכָל־מִמֶּ֖נּוּ אָכָֽלְתָּ׃

i18n.en: He said, "Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree of which I commanded you not to eat?"
i18n.he: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מִ֚י הִגִּ֣יד לְךָ֔ כִּ֥י עֵירֹ֖ם אָ֑תָּה הֲמִן־הָעֵ֗ץ אֲשֶׁ֧ר צִוִּיתִ֛יךָ לְבִלְתִּ֥י אֲכָל־מִמֶּ֖נּוּ אָכָֽלְתָּ׃
i18n.de: Er sprach: "Wer hat dir gesagt, daß du nackt bist? Hast du vom Baum gegessen, von dem ich dir geboten hatte, nicht zu essen?"
i18n.es: Él dijo: «¿Quién te ha dicho que estabas desnudo? ¿Has comido del árbol del que te ordené no comer?»
i18n.fr: Il dit : « Qui t'a dit que tu étais nu ? Aurais-tu mangé de l'arbre dont je t'avais commandé de ne pas manger ? »
i18n.ja: 言った、「誰がお前に、お前が裸であると告げたのか。お前が食べてはならないと命じた木から、お前は食べたのか」。
i18n.ko: 그가 말씀하셨다, "누가 너에게 네가 벗었다고 일러 주었느냐? 내가 너에게 먹지 말라고 명한 그 나무에서 네가 먹었느냐?"
i18n.ru: И сказали они: «Кто сказал тебе, что ты наг? Не ел ли ты от дерева, от которого Я заповедал тебе не есть?»
i18n.zh: 他说：「谁告诉你你是赤身露体的？我吩咐你不可吃的那树上的果子，你吃了吗？」
i18n.zh-Hant: 祂說：「誰告訴你你是赤身的？我吩咐你不可吃的那樹上的果子，你吃了嗎？」

notes.official: The two questions are not requests for information. *Who told you that you were naked?* — the deity is not learning the fact but exposing that the human's new self-consciousness has a source, and that source is the forbidden knowledge. The second question, *Have you eaten from the tree…?*, moves from symptom to act. The interrogation runs backward from the shame to the deed, the way the whole scene diagnoses the transgression from its effects rather than announcing it outright.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הָֽאָדָ֑ם הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣תָּה עִמָּדִ֔י הִ֛וא נָֽתְנָה־לִּ֥י מִן־הָעֵ֖ץ וָאֹכֵֽל׃

i18n.en: The human said, "The woman whom you gave to be with me — she gave me from the tree, and I ate."
i18n.he: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הָֽאָדָ֑ם הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣תָּה עִמָּדִ֔י הִ֛וא נָֽתְנָה־לִּ֥י מִן־הָעֵ֖ץ וָאֹכֵֽל׃
i18n.de: Der Mensch sprach: "Die Frau, die du mir zur Seite gegeben hast — sie gab mir vom Baum, und ich aß."
i18n.es: El ser humano dijo: «La mujer que pusiste para que estuviera conmigo—ella me dio del árbol, y comí».
i18n.fr: L'être humain dit : « La femme que tu m'as donnée pour être avec moi — elle m'a donné de l'arbre, et j'ai mangé. »
i18n.ja: 人は言った、「あなたがわたしと共におらせてくださった女——彼女がその木から取ってわたしに与えたので、わたしは食べたのです」。
i18n.ko: 사람이 말하였다, "당신이 저와 함께 있게 하신 그 여자 — 그녀가 그 나무에서 저에게 주어 제가 먹었습니다."
i18n.ru: И сказал человек: «Женщина, которую Ты дал быть со мною,—она дала мне от дерева, и я ел».
i18n.zh: 那人说：「你赐给我、与我同在的那女人——她把那树上的果子给我，我就吃了。」
i18n.zh-Hant: 那人說：「祢賜給我與我同在的女人—她從那樹上給了我，我就吃了。」

notes.official: **The first deflection.** The human's reply has two interlocutors in it: he answers YHWH-Elohim by gesturing past the woman to *the one who gave him the woman*. The construction is grammatically tight (the relative clause אֲשֶׁר נָתַתָּה עִמָּדִי 'whom you gave to be with me' modifies *the woman*) and rhetorically loose (the implied agency is YHWH-Elohim's). The human admits eating but locates the fault upstream — first in the woman, then in the gift-giver. The structure of blame-deflection is set; the woman will deflect to the serpent in the next verse, and the serpent will receive judgment with no deflection available to him.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים לָאִשָּׁ֖ה מַה־זֹּ֣את עָשִׂ֑ית וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה הַנָּחָ֥שׁ הִשִּׁיאַ֖נִי וָאֹכֵֽל׃

i18n.en: YHWH-Elohim said to the woman, "What is this you have done?" And the woman said, "The serpent deceived me, and I ate."
i18n.he: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים לָאִשָּׁ֖ה מַה־זֹּ֣את עָשִׂ֑ית וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה הַנָּחָ֥שׁ הִשִּׁיאַ֖נִי וָאֹכֵֽל׃
i18n.de: YHWH Elohim sprachen zur Frau: "Was hast du da getan?" Und die Frau sprach: "Die Schlange hat mich getäuscht, und ich aß."
i18n.es: YHWH Elohim dijo a la mujer: «¿Qué es esto que has hecho?» Y la mujer dijo: «La serpiente me engañó, y comí».
i18n.fr: YHWH Elohim dit à la femme : « Qu'est-ce que tu as fait là ? » Et la femme dit : « Le serpent m'a trompée, et j'ai mangé. »
i18n.ja: YHWH エロヒムは女に言った、「お前がしたことは何か」。女は言った、「蛇がわたしを欺いたので、わたしは食べたのです」。
i18n.ko: YHWH 엘로힘이 여자에게 말씀하셨다, "네가 한 이 일이 무엇이냐?" 그러자 여자가 말하였다, "뱀이 저를 속여, 제가 먹었습니다."
i18n.ru: И сказали YHWH Элохим женщине: «Что это ты сделала?» И сказала женщина: «Змей обманул меня, и я ела».
i18n.zh: YHWH 厄罗音对女人说：「你做的是什么事？」女人说：「那蛇欺哄了我，我就吃了。」
i18n.zh-Hant: YHWH 厄羅音對女人說：「你做的這是甚麼事呢？」女人說：「蛇欺哄了我，我就吃了。」

notes.official: **The second deflection completes the chain.** As the human passed responsibility to the woman — and past her, to the maker who gave her (v12) — the woman passes it to the serpent: *the serpent deceived me, and I ate*. The verb הִשִּׁיאַנִי *hishiani* (from נשא, "beguile, deceive") is stronger than the human's bare "she gave me": she at least names deception rather than mere provision. The blame runs downhill in order of address — human, woman, serpent — and the sentences that follow (vv. 14–19) run back up it in reverse, condemning the serpent first. *Hishiani* is the verb the later tradition fastens on (echoed at 2 Cor 11:3 and 1 Tim 2:14).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֥ים ׀ אֶֽל־הַנָּחָשׁ֮ כִּ֣י עָשִׂ֣יתָ זֹּאת֒ אָר֤וּר אַתָּה֙ מִכָּל־הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה וּמִכֹּ֖ל חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה עַל־גְּחֹנְךָ֣ תֵלֵ֔ךְ וְעָפָ֥ר תֹּאכַ֖ל כָּל־יְמֵ֥י חַיֶּֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: YHWH-Elohim said to the serpent, "Because you have done this, cursed are you above all cattle and above every wild animal of the field; on your belly you shall go, and dust you shall eat all the days of your life.
i18n.he: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֥ים ׀ אֶֽל־הַנָּחָשׁ֮ כִּ֣י עָשִׂ֣יתָ זֹּאת֒ אָר֤וּר אַתָּה֙ מִכָּל־הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה וּמִכֹּ֖ל חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה עַל־גְּחֹנְךָ֣ תֵלֵ֔ךְ וְעָפָ֥ר תֹּאכַ֖ל כָּל־יְמֵ֥י חַיֶּֽיךָ׃
i18n.de: YHWH Elohim sprachen zur Schlange: "Weil du dies getan hast, verflucht sollst du sein vor allem Vieh und vor jedem Wildtier des Feldes; auf deinem Bauch sollst du gehen, und Staub sollst du fressen alle Tage deines Lebens.
i18n.es: YHWH Elohim dijo a la serpiente: «Porque has hecho esto, maldita seas entre todo el ganado y entre todo animal salvaje del campo; sobre tu vientre andarás, y polvo comerás todos los días de tu vida.
i18n.fr: YHWH Elohim dit au serpent : « Parce que tu as fait cela, maudit es-tu entre tout le bétail et toute bête sauvage des champs ; sur ton ventre tu iras, et de la poussière tu mangeras tous les jours de ta vie.
i18n.ja: YHWH エロヒムは蛇に言った、「お前がこれをしたゆえに、お前はすべての家畜、また野のすべての獣のうちで呪われる。お前は腹で這い、お前の命のすべての日のあいだ、塵を食べるであろう。
i18n.ko: YHWH 엘로힘이 뱀에게 말씀하셨다, "네가 이 일을 하였으니, 너는 모든 가축과 들의 모든 짐승보다 더 저주를 받았다; 너는 배로 다닐 것이며, 평생 동안 흙을 먹을 것이다.
i18n.ru: И сказали YHWH Элохим змею: «За то, что ты сделал это, проклят ты больше всякого скота и больше всякого дикого животного полевого; на чреве твоём будешь ходить, и прах будешь есть во все дни жизни твоей.
i18n.zh: YHWH 厄罗音对蛇说：「你既做了这事，你必受咒诅，过于一切牲畜，过于田野的一切走兽；你必用肚腹行走，终身吃土。
i18n.zh-Hant: YHWH 厄羅音對蛇說：「因你做了這事，你必受咒詛，比一切牲畜、比田野中的各樣野獸更甚；你要用腹行走，你一生的日子都要吃塵土。

notes.official: *Arur attah* — **cursed are you**. The serpent receives the curse formula directly, the only one of the three to do so. The judgment has two parts: posture (belly-locomotion, dust-eating) and the enmity-clause that follows in v15. The dust-eating is etiological — explaining why snakes appear belly-down — and rhetorical: the serpent feeds on the same substance the human came from (*afar* of 2:7, repeated in 3:19's 'dust you are, and to dust you shall return'). The three are now tied by dust: the human came from it and returns to it; the serpent eats it. The garden's hierarchy has reorganized around the material.

paragraphs.text: וְאֵיבָ֣ה ׀ אָשִׁ֗ית בֵּֽינְךָ֙ וּבֵ֣ין הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וּבֵ֥ין זַרְעֲךָ֖ וּבֵ֣ין זַרְעָ֑הּ ה֚וּא יְשׁוּפְךָ֣ רֹ֔אשׁ וְאַתָּ֖ה תְּשׁוּפֶ֥נּוּ עָקֵֽב׃ (ס)

i18n.en: I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed; he will strike you at the head, and you will strike him at the heel."
i18n.he: וְאֵיבָ֣ה ׀ אָשִׁ֗ית בֵּֽינְךָ֙ וּבֵ֣ין הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וּבֵ֥ין זַרְעֲךָ֖ וּבֵ֣ין זַרְעָ֑הּ ה֚וּא יְשׁוּפְךָ֣ רֹ֔אשׁ וְאַתָּ֖ה תְּשׁוּפֶ֥נּוּ עָקֵֽב׃ (ס)
i18n.de: Und ich will Feindschaft setzen zwischen dir und der Frau und zwischen deinem Samen und ihrem Samen; er wird dir den Kopf zerschlagen, und du wirst ihm die Ferse zerschlagen."
i18n.es: Pondré enemistad entre ti y la mujer, y entre tu simiente y su simiente; él te herirá en la cabeza, y tú lo herirás en el talón».
i18n.fr: Je mettrai inimitié entre toi et la femme, entre ta semence et sa semence ; lui te frappera à la tête, et toi tu le frapperas au talon. »
i18n.ja: わたしはお前と女とのあいだ、お前の子孫と彼女の子孫とのあいだに敵意を置く。彼はお前の頭を打ち、お前は彼のかかとを打つであろう」。
i18n.ko: 내가 너와 여자 사이에, 그리고 네 씨와 그녀의 씨 사이에 적의를 두리니; 그가 네 머리를 칠 것이고, 너는 그의 발꿈치를 칠 것이다."
i18n.ru: И положу вражду между тобою и женщиною, и между семенем твоим и семенем её; он поразит тебя в голову, а ты поразишь его в пяту».
i18n.zh: 我又要叫你和女人彼此为仇，你的后裔与她的后裔也彼此为仇；他要打你的头，你要打他的脚跟。」
i18n.zh-Hant: 我要使你和女人彼此為敵，使你的後裔與她的後裔互相為敵；他要打擊你的頭，你要打擊他的腳跟。」

notes.official:
**Head and heel.** The verb שׁוּף shuf appears only here and in two parallels (Ps 139:11, 'darkness shall *cover* me'; Job 9:17, 'he *crushes* me with a tempest'). The semantic core is contested across 'crush, strike, bruise, lie in wait for'. Both clauses use *the same verb* — whatever the seed does to the serpent's head, the serpent does to the seed's heel. The symmetry argues for a single verb of injurious contact rather than two different actions.

The protoevangelium tradition (Latin: 'the first gospel') reads this verse as a messianic prediction — particularly so via the Vulgate's text-critically dubious *ipsa conteret* 'she shall crush' (with 'she' = Mary). The Hebrew has only הוּא hu 'he' (or 'it', referring back to זֶרַע zera 'seed', a collective). Plenty of Jewish and Christian commentary treats this as etiological — explaining the human-snake antipathy — without the messianic load. WoH renders the symmetry plain and leaves the protoevangelium reading flagged as a separate interpretive tradition.

The ANE backdrop matters: serpent-versus-warrior is a stock combat motif in Mesopotamian and Canaanite mythology. Genesis has demythologized the serpent (he is a *field-animal* now, however cunning), but the head-versus-heel grammar still echoes the older battle.

paragraphs.text: אֶֽל־הָאִשָּׁ֣ה אָמַ֗ר הַרְבָּ֤ה אַרְבֶּה֙ עִצְּבוֹנֵ֣ךְ וְהֵֽרֹנֵ֔ךְ בְּעֶ֖צֶב תֵּֽלְדִ֣י בָנִ֑ים וְאֶל־אִישֵׁךְ֙ תְּשׁ֣וּקָתֵ֔ךְ וְה֖וּא יִמְשָׁל־בָּֽךְ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: To the woman he said, "I will greatly multiply your hardship and your conceiving; in hardship you shall bear children; and your longing shall be for your husband, and he shall rule over you."
i18n.he: אֶֽל־הָאִשָּׁ֣ה אָמַ֗ר הַרְבָּ֤ה אַרְבֶּה֙ עִצְּבוֹנֵ֣ךְ וְהֵֽרֹנֵ֔ךְ בְּעֶ֖צֶב תֵּֽלְדִ֣י בָנִ֑ים וְאֶל־אִישֵׁךְ֙ תְּשׁ֣וּקָתֵ֔ךְ וְה֖וּא יִמְשָׁל־בָּֽךְ׃ (ס)
i18n.de: Zur Frau sprach er: "Ich will deine Mühsal und deine Schwangerschaft sehr mehren; in Mühsal sollst du Kinder gebären; und dein Verlangen wird nach deinem Mann sein, und er wird über dich herrschen."
i18n.es: A la mujer dijo: «Multiplicaré grandemente tu fatiga y tu preñez; con fatiga darás a luz hijos; y tu deseo será para tu marido, y él se enseñoreará de ti».
i18n.fr: À la femme il dit : « Je multiplierai grandement ta peine et ta grossesse ; dans la peine tu enfanteras des enfants ; ton désir se portera vers ton mari, et lui dominera sur toi. »
i18n.ja: 女に向かって言った、「わたしはお前の苦しみと身ごもりを大いに増す。お前は苦しみのうちに子を産む。そしてお前の願いは夫に向かい、彼はお前を治めるであろう」。
i18n.ko: 여자에게 그가 말씀하셨다, "내가 너의 고통과 너의 임신을 크게 더하리니; 너는 고통 중에 자식을 낳을 것이다; 그리고 너의 갈망은 너의 남편을 향할 것이며, 그는 너를 다스릴 것이다."
i18n.ru: Женщине же сказали: «Умножая умножу скорбь твою и беременность твою; в скорби будешь рождать детей; и к мужу твоему будет влечение твоё, и он будет господствовать над тобою».
i18n.zh: 他对女人说：「我必大大增加你的痛苦与你的怀胎；你必在痛苦中生产儿女；你的恋慕必归向你的丈夫，他必管辖你。」
i18n.zh-Hant: 祂對女人說：「我要大大增加你懷胎的艱苦；你要在艱苦中生兒育女；你的渴慕必歸向你的丈夫，他必管轄你。」

notes.official:
**Two phrases, one structural detail.**

First, *itzavon* and *etzev* — both from the same root (עצב), both rendered *hardship*. The woman receives the *same word* for childbearing that the human will receive in v17 for working the ground. The two parallel curses pair: human-and-ground, woman-and-childbearing, bound by the same hardship-noun.

Second, *t'shuqah* and *yimshal* — your longing shall be for your husband, and he shall rule over you. The same construction reappears in 4:7, where sin's *t'shuqah* is for Cain and Cain *must rule* over it. The 4:7 parallel turns the v16 verse darker: not a tender longing but a contested impulse, with the rule-clause as countervailing rather than complementary. WoH renders 'longing' as the most semantically minimal English option and lets the parallel speak in commentary.

Structural note: the woman does not receive the curse formula אֲרוּרָה arurah (as the serpent does in v14 and the ground does in v17). She is told what is *intensified* (childbearing-hardship) and what the new relational dynamic will be (longing-and-rule), but the explicit curse word is reserved.

paragraphs.text: וּלְאָדָ֣ם אָמַ֗ר כִּֽי־שָׁמַעְתָּ֮ לְק֣וֹל אִשְׁתֶּךָ֒ וַתֹּ֙אכַל֙ מִן־הָעֵ֔ץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר צִוִּיתִ֙יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֥א תֹאכַ֖ל מִמֶּ֑נּוּ אֲרוּרָ֤ה הָֽאֲדָמָה֙ בַּֽעֲבוּרֶ֔ךָ בְּעִצָּבוֹן֙ תֹּֽאכֲלֶ֔נָּה כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיֶּֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: And to the human he said, "Because you have listened to the voice of your woman and have eaten from the tree of which I commanded you, saying, 'You shall not eat from it' — cursed is the ground because of you; in hardship you shall eat of it all the days of your life.
i18n.he: וּלְאָדָ֣ם אָמַ֗ר כִּֽי־שָׁמַעְתָּ֮ לְק֣וֹל אִשְׁתֶּךָ֒ וַתֹּ֙אכַל֙ מִן־הָעֵ֔ץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר צִוִּיתִ֙יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֥א תֹאכַ֖ל מִמֶּ֑נּוּ אֲרוּרָ֤ה הָֽאֲדָמָה֙ בַּֽעֲבוּרֶ֔ךָ בְּעִצָּבוֹן֙ תֹּֽאכֲלֶ֔נָּה כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיֶּֽיךָ׃
i18n.de: Und zum Menschen sprach er: "Weil du auf die Stimme deiner Frau gehört und vom Baum gegessen hast, von dem ich dir geboten hatte und sprach: 'Du sollst nicht von ihm essen' — verflucht sei der Ackerboden um deinetwillen; in Mühsal sollst du von ihm essen alle Tage deines Lebens.
i18n.es: Y al ser humano dijo: «Porque has escuchado la voz de tu mujer y has comido del árbol del que te ordené, diciendo: ‹No comerás de él›—maldito sea el suelo por tu causa; con fatiga comerás de él todos los días de tu vida.
i18n.fr: Et à l'être humain il dit : « Parce que tu as écouté la voix de ta femme et que tu as mangé de l'arbre dont je t'avais commandé, en disant : “Tu n'en mangeras pas” — maudit soit le sol à cause de toi ; dans la peine tu en mangeras tous les jours de ta vie.
i18n.ja: そして人に向かって言った、「お前は自分の女の声に聞き従い、わたしが『お前はそれから食べてはならない』と命じた木から食べたゆえに——お前のゆえに大地は呪われる。お前は命のすべての日のあいだ、苦しみのうちにそれから食べるであろう。
i18n.ko: 그리고 사람에게 그가 말씀하셨다, "네가 네 여자의 소리를 듣고, 내가 너에게 명하여 '그것에서 먹지 말라' 하던 그 나무에서 먹었으니 — 너로 인하여 땅이 저주받았다; 너는 평생 동안 고통 중에 그것에서 먹을 것이다.
i18n.ru: А человеку сказали: «За то, что ты послушался голоса жены твоей и ел от дерева, о котором Я заповедал тебе, говоря: ‘Не ешь от него’,—проклята земля из-за тебя; в скорби будешь есть от неё во все дни жизни твоей.
i18n.zh: 他又对那人说：「你既听从了你女人的声音，吃了我吩咐你不可吃的那树上的果子——为你的缘故，大地受咒诅；你必终身在痛苦中从大地得吃的。
i18n.zh-Hant: 祂對那人說：「因你聽從了你女人的聲音，吃了我吩咐你不可吃的那樹上的果子—為你的緣故，大地受咒詛；你一生的日子都要在艱苦中從中得吃的。

notes.official:
**The curse falls on the ground, not on the human.** *Arurah ha-adamah ba-avurecha* — 'cursed is the ground because of you'. Read precisely: of the three speeches in v14–19, the serpent is cursed (v14, *arur attah* 'cursed are you'), the ground is cursed (v17, *arurah ha-adamah* 'cursed is the ground'), but the *human* is not. The text refuses to use the curse formula on him directly. He is told *the ground he came from* is now cursed *on his account* (בַּעֲבוּרֶךָ ba-avurecha). His relation to the adamah turns adversarial — itzavon now mediates the bond — but he himself is not pronounced cursed.

This structural restraint is theologically significant. The traditional reading sometimes speaks of 'the curse on humanity'; the text speaks of a curse on the *ground* and a hardship-relationship between human and ground. The mortality-clause that follows in v19 ('dust you are, and to dust you shall return') is etiology, not curse: it names what the human always was and what he therefore returns to.

paragraphs.text: וְק֥וֹץ וְדַרְדַּ֖ר תַּצְמִ֣יחַֽ לָ֑ךְ וְאָכַלְתָּ֖ אֶת־עֵ֥שֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃

i18n.en: It shall sprout thorns and thistles for you; and you shall eat the herb of the field.
i18n.he: וְק֥וֹץ וְדַרְדַּ֖ר תַּצְמִ֣יחַֽ לָ֑ךְ וְאָכַלְתָּ֖ אֶת־עֵ֥שֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃
i18n.de: Dornen und Disteln wird er dir aufsprossen lassen; und du wirst das Kraut des Feldes essen.
i18n.es: Espinos y cardos te hará brotar; y comerás la hierba del campo.
i18n.fr: Il fera germer pour toi épines et chardons ; et tu mangeras l'herbe des champs.
i18n.ja: 大地はお前のために茨とあざみを生やし、お前は野の草を食べるであろう。
i18n.ko: 그것이 너에게 가시와 엉겅퀴를 돋게 할 것이며; 너는 들의 풀을 먹을 것이다.
i18n.ru: Тернии и волчцы произрастит она тебе; и будешь есть траву полевую.
i18n.zh: 大地必为你长出荆棘与蒺藜；你必吃田间的草木。
i18n.zh-Hant: 大地必為你長出荊棘與蒺藜；你要吃田野中的草本。

notes.official: *Qots ve-dardar* — **thorns and thistles**. The ground's answer to the human's labour will be resistance, not only food; the pair is a hendiadys for hostile scrub. It marks the move from the garden — where every tree "desirable to the sight and good for food" grew (2:9) — to open country, where sustenance must be forced from soil that fights back. And the diet moves with it: *you shall eat the esev ha-sadeh*, **the plant of the field** — the very category 2:5 said could not grow until there was rain and a human to till it. The human now becomes that tiller, eating the rain-and-labour crop by the sweat of v19. The arc is long and deliberate: from the freely given seed-plants and fruit of 1:29 and the garden's trees, down to the toil-grown field-herbage of the world outside. The vegetarian diet persists; its ease is gone.

paragraphs.text: בְּזֵעַ֤ת אַפֶּ֙יךָ֙ תֹּ֣אכַל לֶ֔חֶם עַ֤ד שֽׁוּבְךָ֙ אֶל־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה כִּ֥י מִמֶּ֖נָּה לֻקָּ֑חְתָּ כִּֽי־עָפָ֣ר אַ֔תָּה וְאֶל־עָפָ֖ר תָּשֽׁוּב׃

i18n.en: By the sweat of your face you shall eat bread until you return to the ground, for from it you were taken; for you are dust, and to dust you shall return.
i18n.he: בְּזֵעַ֤ת אַפֶּ֙יךָ֙ תֹּ֣אכַל לֶ֔חֶם עַ֤ד שֽׁוּבְךָ֙ אֶל־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה כִּ֥י מִמֶּ֖נָּה לֻקָּ֑חְתָּ כִּֽי־עָפָ֣ר אַ֔תָּה וְאֶל־עָפָ֖ר תָּשֽׁוּב׃
i18n.de: Im Schweiße deines Angesichts sollst du Brot essen, bis du zum Ackerboden zurückkehrst, denn von ihm bist du genommen; denn Staub bist du, und zum Staub sollst du zurückkehren.
i18n.es: Con el sudor de tu rostro comerás pan hasta que vuelvas al suelo, pues de él fuiste tomado; porque polvo eres, y al polvo volverás».
i18n.fr: À la sueur de ton visage tu mangeras du pain, jusqu'à ce que tu retournes au sol, car de lui tu as été pris ; car tu es poussière, et à la poussière tu retourneras. »
i18n.ja: お前は顔に汗して、パンを食べることになる、お前が大地に帰るまで。なぜなら、お前はそこから取られたからである。お前は塵であり、塵に帰るのである」。
i18n.ko: 너는 얼굴에 땀을 흘려 빵을 먹을 것이니, 네가 땅으로 돌아갈 때까지 그러하리라, 네가 거기에서 취하여졌기 때문이다; 너는 흙이니, 흙으로 돌아갈 것이다."
i18n.ru: В поте лица твоего будешь есть хлеб, доколе не возвратишься в землю, ибо из неё ты взят; ибо прах ты, и в прах возвратишься».
i18n.zh: 你必汗流满面才得吃饭，直到你归回大地，因为你是从那里被取出来的；你本是尘土，仍要归于尘土。」
i18n.zh-Hant: 你必汗流滿面才能吃到糧食，直到你歸回土壤，因為你是從其中取出來的；你本是塵土，仍要歸回塵土。」

notes.official: *Ki afar attah v'el afar tashuv* — **for you are dust, and to dust you shall return**. The closing line of the human's speech is not announcing a new fate but stating the standing one. *Afar* 'dust' is the same word as in 2:7, where the human was formed from dust of the ground. The verse closes the etymological arc: dust → human → dust. *Mot tamut* 'you shall surely die' (2:17) is here unfolded — not as a single-day execution but as the now-active condition of mortality. The garden suspended this trajectory by giving access to the tree of life (v22 will name it explicitly); the chapter's ending removes that access.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְרָ֧א הָֽאָדָ֛ם שֵׁ֥ם אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ חַוָּ֑ה כִּ֛י הִ֥וא הָֽיְתָ֖ה אֵ֥ם כָּל־חָֽי׃

i18n.en: The human called his woman's name Chavvah, because she became the mother of all living.
i18n.he: וַיִּקְרָ֧א הָֽאָדָ֛ם שֵׁ֥ם אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ חַוָּ֑ה כִּ֛י הִ֥וא הָֽיְתָ֖ה אֵ֥ם כָּל־חָֽי׃
i18n.de: Der Mensch nannte den Namen seiner Frau Chawwa, denn sie wurde die Mutter alles Lebendigen.
i18n.es: El ser humano llamó el nombre de su mujer Chavvah, porque fue la madre de todo viviente.
i18n.fr: L'être humain appela le nom de sa femme Chavvah, parce qu'elle devint la mère de tout vivant.
i18n.ja: 人はその女の名をハヴァと呼んだ。なぜなら、彼女がすべての生ける者の母となったからである。
i18n.ko: 사람은 자기 여자의 이름을 하와라 불렀으니, 그녀가 모든 산 자의 어머니가 되었기 때문이다.
i18n.ru: И назвал человек имя жены своей Хавва, ибо она стала матерью всех живущих.
i18n.zh: 那人给他的女人起名叫夏娃，因为她要成为众生之母。
i18n.zh-Hant: 那人給他的女人取名為哈娃，因為她成了眾生之母。

notes.official: **The third naming.** The species was named *adam* by the Elohim (1:26–27); the gender-counterpart was named *Ishah* by the human (2:23); now in 3:20 the human gives his woman a personal name — *Chavvah*, glossed by the verse as connected to *chai* 'living, life'. The naming comes *after* the death-prediction of v19, and against it. The human's first interpretive act in the post-garden world names his woman not by mortality but by life. The English form *Eve* derives via the LXX (Εὕα) and Vulgate (Eva); WoH keeps the Hebrew *Chavvah* so the chai-resonance is visible.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּעַשׂ֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֜ים לְאָדָ֧ם וּלְאִשְׁתּ֛וֹ כָּתְנ֥וֹת ע֖וֹר וַיַּלְבִּשֵֽׁם׃ (פ)

i18n.en: YHWH-Elohim made for the human and his woman garments of skin, and clothed them.
i18n.he: וַיַּעַשׂ֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֜ים לְאָדָ֧ם וּלְאִשְׁתּ֛וֹ כָּתְנ֥וֹת ע֖וֹר וַיַּלְבִּשֵֽׁם׃ (פ)
i18n.de: YHWH Elohim machten dem Menschen und seiner Frau Kleider aus Fell und kleideten sie.
i18n.es: YHWH Elohim hizo para el ser humano y para su mujer túnicas de piel, y los vistió.
i18n.fr: YHWH Elohim fit pour l'être humain et sa femme des tuniques de peau, et les en revêtit.
i18n.ja: YHWH エロヒムは人とその女のために皮の衣を造り、これを彼らに着せた。
i18n.ko: YHWH 엘로힘이 사람과 그의 여자를 위하여 가죽옷을 만들어 그들에게 입히셨다.
i18n.ru: И сделали YHWH Элохим человеку и жене его одежды из кожи, и одели их.
i18n.zh: YHWH 厄罗音为那人和他的女人作了皮衣，给他们穿上。
i18n.zh-Hant: YHWH 厄羅音為那人和他的女人作了皮衣，給他們穿上。

notes.official: **An upgrade from improvisation.** The fig-leaf belts of v7 are replaced with full-coverage tunics of hide. The verse is given in three terse verbs: *made … garments … clothed*. The text is silent on where the skins came from — the first implied animal death in Genesis sits in this gap. Tradition has filled it in many ways; the text refuses to. What is recorded is the *act of clothing* — YHWH-Elohim dresses them himself, on the way out of the garden. Whatever else the gesture is, it is not abandonment.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ׀ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֗ים הֵ֤ן הָֽאָדָם֙ הָיָה֙ כְּאַחַ֣ד מִמֶּ֔נּוּ לָדַ֖עַת ט֣וֹב וָרָ֑ע וְעַתָּ֣ה ׀ פֶּן־יִשְׁלַ֣ח יָד֗וֹ וְלָקַח֙ גַּ֚ם מֵעֵ֣ץ הַֽחַיִּ֔ים וְאָכַ֖ל וָחַ֥י לְעֹלָֽם׃

i18n.en: YHWH-Elohim said, "Behold, the human has become like one of us, knowing good and bad. And now, lest he reach out his hand and take also from the tree of life, and eat, and live forever—"
i18n.he: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ׀ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֗ים הֵ֤ן הָֽאָדָם֙ הָיָה֙ כְּאַחַ֣ד מִמֶּ֔נּוּ לָדַ֖עַת ט֣וֹב וָרָ֑ע וְעַתָּ֣ה ׀ פֶּן־יִשְׁלַ֣ח יָד֗וֹ וְלָקַח֙ גַּ֚ם מֵעֵ֣ץ הַֽחַיִּ֔ים וְאָכַ֖ל וָחַ֥י לְעֹלָֽם׃
i18n.de: YHWH Elohim sprachen: "Siehe, der Mensch ist geworden wie einer von uns, erkennend Gut und Böse. Und nun, daß er nicht seine Hand ausstrecke und auch vom Baum des Lebens nehme und esse und ewig lebe —"
i18n.es: YHWH Elohim dijo: «He aquí, el ser humano ha venido a ser como uno de nosotros, conociendo el bien y el mal. Y ahora, no sea que extienda su mano y tome también del árbol de la vida, y coma, y viva para siempre—»
i18n.fr: YHWH Elohim dit : « Voici, l'être humain est devenu comme l'un d'entre nous, connaissant le bien et le mal. Et maintenant, qu'il n'étende pas la main et ne prenne aussi de l'arbre de vie, et qu'il n'en mange et ne vive à jamais — »
i18n.ja: YHWH エロヒムは言った、「見よ、人は善悪を知ることにおいて、われわれのひとりのようになった。今や、彼が手を伸ばして命の木からも取り、食べて、永遠に生きることのないように——」。
i18n.ko: YHWH 엘로힘이 말씀하셨다, "보라, 사람이 우리 중 하나처럼 되어, 선악을 알게 되었다. 이제 그가 손을 내밀어 생명의 나무에서도 따 먹고 영원히 살까 하노라 —"
i18n.ru: И сказали YHWH Элохим: «Вот, человек стал как один из нас, знающий добро и зло. А теперь, как бы он не простёр руки своей и не взял также от дерева жизни, и не съел, и не стал жить вечно—»
i18n.zh: YHWH 厄罗音说：「看哪，那人已经如同我们当中之一，认知善恶。现在，恐怕他伸手又摘生命树的果子吃了，就永远活着——」
i18n.zh-Hant: YHWH 厄羅音說：「看哪，那人已成為如我們當中之一，能認知善惡。如今，恐怕他伸手又從生命之樹摘取吃了，便永遠活著—」

notes.official:
**The second explicit divine plural.** The first was 1:26 ('let us make humankind in our image'); this is the second. Both pivot on what humans share with the speaker(s). In 1:26 the Elohim made humankind in *their* (the Elohim-class') image; in 3:22 the human has — by the eating — become *like one of them*, specifically in the domain of *knowing good and bad*. The serpent's promise (v5) is now confirmed from the divine side using the exact same vocabulary.

Three observations.

First, the speech is *internal to the Elohim-class*: YHWH-Elohim is speaking to other members (the *us*), not to the human. The chapter's framing here is closer to a council deliberation than a pronouncement.

Second, the speech is grammatically *incomplete*: 'lest he reach out his hand and take also from the tree of life, and eat, and live forever—' has no apodosis. The sentence stops; the next verse acts. YHWH-Elohim doesn't finish the sentence because the action *is* the finish.

Third, the threat motivating the expulsion is not punishment but *limit-keeping*: if the human, now in possession of the knowing-good-and-bad, also gains access to perpetual life, the class-rise the serpent promised completes. The expulsion is to keep the boundary — to prevent a full join into the Elohim-class. The garden contained both trees; only the tree of life is now made inaccessible. The knowing-tree is no longer dangerous because its fruit has already been eaten.

paragraphs.text: וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵ֛הוּ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים מִגַּן־עֵ֑דֶן לַֽעֲבֹד֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֻקַּ֖ח מִשָּֽׁם׃

i18n.en: So YHWH-Elohim sent him out of the garden of Eden, to work the ground from which he had been taken.
i18n.he: וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵ֛הוּ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים מִגַּן־עֵ֑דֶן לַֽעֲבֹד֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֻקַּ֖ח מִשָּֽׁם׃
i18n.de: So sandten YHWH Elohim ihn fort aus dem Garten Eden, den Ackerboden zu bearbeiten, aus dem er genommen war.
i18n.es: Y YHWH Elohim lo envió fuera del jardín de Edén, para labrar el suelo del cual había sido tomado.
i18n.fr: Aussi YHWH Elohim le renvoya du jardin d'Éden, pour travailler le sol d'où il avait été pris.
i18n.ja: そこで YHWH エロヒムは、彼が取られた大地を耕させるために、エデンの園から彼を送り出した。
i18n.ko: 그래서 YHWH 엘로힘이 그를 에덴 동산에서 내보내어, 그가 거기에서 취하여진 땅을 일구게 하셨다.
i18n.ru: И выслали YHWH Элохим его из сада Эденского, чтобы возделывать землю, из которой он был взят.
i18n.zh: 于是 YHWH 厄罗音把他从伊甸园中送出去，去耕作他从那里被取出来的可耕之地。
i18n.zh-Hant: 於是 YHWH 厄羅音將他從伊甸園中送出去，去耕作他從中被取出的土壤。

notes.official: **The work of v15 of chapter 2 continues, but outside.** The human was placed in the garden 'to work it and to guard it' (2:15, לְעָבְדָהּ וּלְשָׁמְרָהּ). He is now sent to *work the ground* (לַעֲבֹד אֶת־הָאֲדָמָה) — the same verb עָבַד avad, but the object has shifted from *the garden* (or *the adamah*-of-the-garden) to *the adamah* in general, the cursed-because-of-him ground of v17. The work continues; its conditions change. The original mandate is not revoked, only relocated.

paragraphs.text: וַיְגָ֖רֶשׁ אֶת־הָֽאָדָ֑ם וַיַּשְׁכֵּן֩ מִקֶּ֨דֶם לְגַן־עֵ֜דֶן אֶת־הַכְּרֻבִ֗ים וְאֵ֨ת לַ֤הַט הַחֶ֙רֶב֙ הַמִּתְהַפֶּ֔כֶת לִשְׁמֹ֕ר אֶת־דֶּ֖רֶךְ עֵ֥ץ הַֽחַיִּֽים׃ (ס)

i18n.en: He drove out the human, and placed at the east of the garden of Eden the cherubim and the flaming blade that turns itself, to guard the way to the tree of life.
i18n.he: וַיְגָ֖רֶשׁ אֶת־הָֽאָדָ֑ם וַיַּשְׁכֵּן֩ מִקֶּ֨דֶם לְגַן־עֵ֜דֶן אֶת־הַכְּרֻבִ֗ים וְאֵ֨ת לַ֤הַט הַחֶ֙רֶב֙ הַמִּתְהַפֶּ֔כֶת לִשְׁמֹ֕ר אֶת־דֶּ֖רֶךְ עֵ֥ץ הַֽחַיִּֽים׃ (ס)
i18n.de: Sie vertrieben den Menschen und setzten östlich vor den Garten Eden die Kerubim und die flammende Klinge, die sich wendet, um den Weg zum Baum des Lebens zu hüten.
i18n.es: Echó fuera al ser humano, y colocó al oriente del jardín de Edén los querubines y la espada llameante que se revuelve, para guardar el camino al árbol de la vida.
i18n.fr: Il chassa l'être humain, et plaça à l'orient du jardin d'Éden les chérubins et la flamme de l'épée qui tournoie, pour garder le chemin de l'arbre de vie.
i18n.ja: 彼は人を追い出し、エデンの園の東にケルビムと、ひるがえる炎の剣を置き、命の木への道を守らせた。
i18n.ko: 그가 사람을 쫓아내시고, 에덴 동산 동쪽에 케루빔과 회전하는 불칼을 두어 생명의 나무로 가는 길을 지키게 하셨다.
i18n.ru: И изгнали человека и поставили на востоке сада Эденского керувим и пламенное лезвие меча обращающееся, чтобы охранять путь к дереву жизни.
i18n.zh: 他赶逐了那人，又在伊甸园的东边安设了基路冰，以及四面旋转的火焰之剑，把守通往生命树的道路。
i18n.zh-Hant: 祂驅逐了那人，並在伊甸園的東邊安置了基路冰，以及那旋轉的火焰之劍，把守通往生命之樹的道路。

notes.official:
**Two guardians, one access denied.** *K'ruvim* are the composite hybrid figures of ANE iconography — winged sphinxes flanking thrones and temple thresholds, not the cherubic putti of later Christian art. They reappear in the Hebrew Bible as the throne-bearers of YHWH (1 Sam 4:4, Ezek 10), as flanking the Ark (Ex 25:18), as a temple-throne motif (1 Kgs 6:23–28). Here, plural, they take up station at the garden's eastern approach.

*Lahat ha-cherev ha-mithappechet* — **the flaming blade that turns itself**. The hithpael participle *mithappechet* gives the blade autonomous motion: it *turns itself*, not 'turned every way' (KJV's vague rendering, which leaves the agent unspecified). The image is striking: an unhanded weapon. Combined with the cherubim, the garden is now protected by two distinct guardians — animate (cherubim) and self-animating (blade). The way *back* to the tree of life is sealed.

The chapter that opened with humans in the garden, naked and unashamed, closes with humans outside the garden, clothed in hide, and the garden's eastern gate guarded against return. The arc from 2:25 to 3:24 has bent decisively. What was begun in 4:1 — childbearing, naming, the first generation outside — will follow.
